leads.title: Whitewood v. Wolf - U.S. District Court ruling
leads.documents: Legalized same-sex marriage in Pennsylvania by striking down statutory ban as unconstitutional
leads.detail: U.S. District Court Judge John E. Jones III ruled May 20, 2014; ACLU filed lawsuit in federal court July 9, 2013; Attorney General Kathleen Kane refused to defend statute

leads.title: Commonwealth v. Bonadio - Supreme Court of Pennsylvania
leads.documents: Found Pennsylvania's sodomy law unconstitutional under equal protection guarantees of state and federal constitutions
leads.detail: 1980 ruling cited; legislation legalized consensual sodomy for heterosexual married couples in 1972; remaining sodomy laws repealed 1995

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, Georgia - U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Ruled discrimination in workplace on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is discrimination on basis of sex under Title VII
leads.detail: Decided June 15, 2020; cited as protecting LGBT employees from workplace discrimination

leads.title: Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission interpretation and regulations under Pennsylvania Human Relations Act
leads.documents: Statewide enforcement machinery banning discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing, education, public accommodations
leads.detail: Interpreted since August 2018 as banned under category of sex; legally-binding regulations added and signed off by Governor Tom Wolf in December 2022 under 'definition of sex' explicitly includes sexual orientation and gender identity

leads.title: HB300 - Pennsylvania House of Representatives bill
leads.documents: Bill to explicitly legally ban discrimination on basis of sexual orientation and gender identity or expression
leads.detail: Formally passed Pennsylvania House April 2023 by vote 102-98; awaits vote within Pennsylvania Senate

leads.title: 18 PA 5903 obscenity statute and July 2022 repeal act
leads.documents: State obscenity law that listed 'acts of homosexuality' as sexual conduct; repeal removed archaic references to homosexuality from criminal code
leads.detail: Cited as 18 PA 5903; Upper Darby 1987 ordinance parallel; two votes May 2021 at Pennsylvania General Assembly to remove failed; bill passed unanimously both houses July 2022 and signed by Governor Tom Wolf effective immediately

leads.title: Pennsylvania Department of Health birth certificate policy and PennDOT X-marker
leads.documents: Requirements for transgender people to change gender on birth certificates and driver's licenses/state IDs
leads.detail: August 2016 change: sex reassignment surgery no longer required, physician note of appropriate clinical treatment required, under-18 needs parental request; Since July 23, 2020 third gender option 'X' on driver's licenses and state IDs but not birth certificates

leads.title: City of Philadelphia gender-identity ordinances and sanctuary executive order - Mayor Jim Kenney
leads.documents: Prohibit youth-serving organizations from discriminating against trans, nonbinary, gender-nonconforming youth; require gender-neutral bathroom in city-owned buildings; clarify Fair Practice Ordinance protects nonbinary/gender-fluid people; sanctuary city status for trans/non-binary access to services
leads.detail: Three ordinances signed November 2019; December 2021 virtual public schools X option; October 2023 officially became 'sanctuary city' via executive order

leads.title: Governor Tom Wolf August 2022 executive order and Pittsburgh conversion therapy ordinance
leads.documents: Bans state-based government funding for conversion therapy; local bans on conversion therapy on minors
leads.detail: Executive order signed August 2022 effective immediately; Pittsburgh first city Dec 14, 2016 passed 9-0 effective Jan 1, 2017; Philadelphia and Allentown July 2017; May 2024 5 health boards implemented statewide healthcare ban

leads.title: Senate Bill 9 'Save Women's Sports Act' and 2022 transgender athlete ban veto
leads.documents: Enforcement risk for trans athletes - mandates athletes play on teams according to gender assigned at birth; prior similar bill passed both houses and vetoed
leads.detail: June 2022 bill to ban transgender athletes passed both houses of Pennsylvania General Assembly, vetoed by Governor Tom Wolf July 2022; Senate approved Senate Bill 9 in May 2025
